chunks: Ali ibn al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: I recited to Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Harith. I said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Khalaf al-Attar narrated to you. He said: Husayn al-Ashqar narrated to us. He said: Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam narrated to us from his father from Said ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. He said:

I asked the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) about the words that Adam received from his Lord by which He forgave him. He said: He asked Him by the right of Muhammad, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, "forgive me," so He forgave him.

key_terms.الكلمات: The words that Adam received from his Lord (Quran 2:37)
key_terms.بحق: By the right of -- invoking intercession through sacred figures
key_terms.فتاب عليه: He accepted his repentance / forgave him

ai.seo_question: What words did Adam receive from God to earn His forgiveness according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Ibn Abbas asked the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) about the identity of the words that Adam (AS) received from his Lord, as mentioned in Quran 2:37. The Prophet explained that Adam invoked God by the right (haqq) of the five members of the Ahl al-Bayt -- Muhammad, Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn -- asking for forgiveness, and God accepted his repentance. This tradition is significant in Shia theology as it connects the exalted status of the Ahl al-Bayt to the earliest event of human history, indicating their pre-eternal honor before God.
